break_it.scenario: The article overstates the legal position — implies NSW conveyancers have a settled statutory duty to provide climate analysis
break_it.what_happens: A reader relies on a false statement of law; the piece becomes misleading and damages the brand's credibility with the exact professional audience it targets
break_it.how: the copy explicitly says NSW has NOT legislated a vendor climate-disclosure duty and frames the duty scope as evolving/prudent-practice, not mandated; Shaddock is cited accurately (information-provider liability for negligent omission); the corporate climate-disclosure standard is described as a signal of direction, not a duty on conveyancers
break_it.repro: read the #direction and #duty sections — each carries an explicit 'this does not bind a residential transaction / does not suggest it has' qualifier

break_it.scenario: The article uses a climate 'score' or 'at risk' verdict, repeating the misleading-conduct pattern the org's own legal review banned (#699)
break_it.what_happens: Property-defamation / misleading-conduct exposure of the same kind that was removed from the live climate tool
break_it.how: the copy states projections should be shown 'as cited, dated context — not as a score or a verdict, which can mislead'; no suburb-level 'will be underwater' claims; liability-word sweep returned zero flagged terms
break_it.repro: grep the page for 'score'/'at risk'/'underwater' — only appears in the negative ('not a score or a verdict')

break_it.scenario: The article claims the report renders coastal/estuarine inundation, which is not yet shipped (data loaded, render pending)
break_it.what_happens: A false product-capability claim; a conveyancer buys expecting a section that isn't there
break_it.how: the CTA lists only LIVE capabilities (LEP/SEPP/DCP controls, flood and bushfire mapping, cited climate projections from merged #702); estuarine inundation is referenced only as a newly published NSW GOVERNMENT dataset a buyer needs, never as a current report feature
break_it.repro: read the CTA block — it names flood, bushfire, climate projections; not coastal/estuarine as a report section
